summary: Customer settlement first slice: settlement of 1..n complete unconsumed approved term rows with term-derived integer amounts and cumulative HALF_UP conservation, active open items split into due/retention partitions, read-only aging pools, six routes/templates, two named read-only cross-owner interfaces, settlement integrity branch and SQLite/PostgreSQL guards. Cash clearing, credit/bad debt, AP, invoices, disputes, reversal and opening items remain future tasks.

deviations: PH-226 (test prerequisite) was merged first so the settlement plugin's contracts/delivery dependency edge does not break two existing SQLite tests and two PostgreSQL concurrency setUp blocks; PH-224 was rebased onto that BASE.

Module-disabled HTTP routes return 403 while settlement history remains readable through the service layer; this matches other plugins and is the intended 'history readable' reading (spec service-layer read, not public route).

Term keys are frozen as coverage_key='term:<due|retention>:<term_id>' and partition_key='<due|retention>:<term_id>' with source_id=contract_line_id, matching the frozen spec semantics despite the earlier 'kind' wording ambiguity.
Settlement evidence refs are restricted to canonical {evidence_id, sha256, kind}; the free-text basis stays in the private terms_snapshot/evidence_note and the UI displays evidence_display.

Browser evidence on final HEAD 9566481: 57/57 checks pass, 0 failures; three defects found and fixed (aging due/release date rendering, source ref readability, draft edit pre-check of selected terms).
unverified: PostgreSQL concurrency/lock/period-race execution is provided by the PR's PostgreSQL CI job; local SQLite skips are not evidence.
Production/customer UAT, cash clearing, credit/bad debt, AP, invoices, disputes, active-settlement reversal, opening items and AgingCase writes are out of this slice.
Browser evidence covers Chromium 320/390/768/1024/1440 only; printing, dark mode, touch and non-Chromium browsers untested.
